Updated assessment with SLOOS insights:
- The FOMC’s cautiously optimistic read—solid labor market, transitory Q1 softness, inflation near target with a gradual path—remains broadly appropriate.
- April 2017 SLOOS points to somewhat mixed-to-softer credit transmission: domestic banks reportedly tightened standards for auto loans while easing some credit card terms and maintaining willingness to lend on consumer installment loans; CRE standards, especially for construction and multifamily, were tighter amid concerns about CRE valuations, capital adequacy, and regulatory changes; C&I loan demand was generally softer, and foreign banks reported higher loan spreads and lower LTVs. 
- These SLOOS signals suggest financial conditions are not uniformly easing through bank credit channels, especially for business and CRE, tempering the otherwise positive labor/inflation backdrop highlighted by the FOMC.

Net effect: keep an overall positive but more balanced tone than before; adjust sentiment modestly lower to reflect mixed bank credit conditions and softer C&I/CRE demand.

sentiment score = 0.50
